patch_description: The original program simply returned random points, yielding a near-zero minimum triangle area. My approach replaces that with a deterministic, vectorized stochastic hill-climb (pattern search with adaptive step sizes) directly on the true objective: the minimum triangle area normalized by the convex hull area. Key insights: (1) all C(13,3)=286 triangle areas can be computed in a single vectorized cross-product operation, making the objective cheap enough for thousands of evaluations per second; (2) the convex hull (computed with a lightweight monotone-chain hull) is the normalization region; (3) boundary-biased initializations (points on an ellipse/regular polygon with slight interior mixing) provide good starting basins, since optimal Heilbronn configurations push points toward the boundary; (4) a fixed seed plus a fixed iteration budget guarantees determinism. Single-point Gaussian perturbations with adaptive shrinking/expanding steps give fine local refinement while remaining robust to the non-smooth min() objective.
